result.title: Travel Back To Move Forward: Retrospective Exploration and Evolving for Long Horizon Agents
result.summary: Large language model agents increasingly operate in long-horizon environments where early mistakes can trigger cascading failures and trap agents in dead-end trajectories. Agents must therefore be able to proactively recover from such states and turn their exploratory experience into guidance for subsequent decisions. We introduce ReTRAIL, a framework that enables agents to rewind the environment to earlier states while preserving valid progress and carrying forward knowledge learned from abandoned exploration. The environment state moves backward while the agent's knowledge continues to move forward. ReTRAIL trains a shared policy with two complementary signals: State-Anchored GRPO compares alternative continuations from revisited states to improve execution, while a branch-advancement reward guides reflection through the progress of subsequent exploration. Experiments across four interactive benchmark MineSweeper, Sokoban, ALFWorld and ScienceWorld show that simply adding a rewind primitive provides limited benefit and can even degrade performance. In contrast, ReTRAIL enables agents to rewind from unproductive states and use insights from abandoned branches to guide subsequent exploration. These results demonstrate the value of coupling environment rewinding with experience reuse within an ongoing task for long-horizon task solving. The code is available at https://github.com/whi497/ReTRAIL.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ReTRAIL 框架：让长时程 LLM agent 在保留有效进展的前提下把环境回退到先前状态，并把被放弃探索分支中学到的知识继续带入后续决策；用两个信号训练共享策略——State-Anchored GRPO 比较同一回访状态下的不同续接，branch-advancement reward 借助后续探索进展引导反思。在 MineSweeper、Sokoban、ALFWorld、ScienceWorld 上验证，发现单纯加入「rewind」原语收益有限甚至有害。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文以回访旧状态、比较多条续接并为其分配奖励的方式做轨迹级信用分配，可能为 LVR 中回溯式状态更新、搜索/验证与轨迹监督提供可迁移线索；但实验均为纯文本交互 agent，如何映射到视觉 latent 推理状态仍需核查。
